items.title: Harold E. Peterson Interview, 1979-08-06
items.q: The name 'Karen' is mentioned by the Interviewer ('Yeah, man it sure was Karen.') but the Interviewee does not respond to or acknowledge Karen, only continuing the conversation about the storm and lost records.

ctx.x: You see, we didn't take, we didn't take all this wood to make this, put it up this, you know, in the back there, racks and all that you could put it up. When we first moved out here, we moved everything, but we, I still stayed in the storm until October the 1st. We moved out here in June. In September we had that storm. And that side of our garage there, one side is the, you got the, well, the slay asbestos, the slates, and the other side is the tapollion, you know. And boy, it just, and not only that, but the…

Yeah, I'd like to have gotten out there and seen your stuff, you know. Gosh. That was such an awful storm. It rained and, come through four floors. Yeah, man, it sure was Karen. And I was wearing my white shampoos.
What a funny thing, man. If I'd left your stuff up on... Yeah. Yeah.
